newsitem.title: CHINA: China to open bidding on $120 mln water plant.
newsitem.headline: China to open bidding on $120 mln water plant.

text.p: China will open its first build-operate-transfer (BOT) water project to bidding by foreign contractors in April or May, the China Daily said on Saturday.

The project to build a fourth phase of a plant in Chengdu in southwestern Sichuan province would cost about one billion yuan ($120 million), the newspaper quoted Zhou Jiang, general manager of Bridge of Trust Infrastructure Investment Consulting Co, as saying.

Chengdu, which was facing an urgent tap water shortfall of 200-300,000 tonnes a day, would buy a set amount of water from the plant but the exact amount had yet to be fixed, said Zhou, whose company is handling the bidding.
The water project would take about two and a half years to complete, Zhou said.

"Investors may be more enthusiastic to invest in power generating projects than in water plants, but the latter require less funding and shorter periods of construction," the newspaper quoted Zhou as saying.
A formal contract with a French consortium for a BOT power plant in the southern region of Guangxi would be signed in May when French President Jacques Chirac is to visit Beijing, Zhou said.
France's state-owned Electricite de France and GEC-Alsthom NV signed a draft contract last November for the $590 million Laibin B coal-fired power station.
Bidding documents for a power plant in Changsha in central Hunan province would be issued in one or two months, Zhou said but did not elaborate.

Two other BOT projects -- a bridge over the Yangtze River in Wuhan and an 80-km highway linking Yangjiang and Dianbai in Guangdong province -- were awaiting final approval by the State Council, or cabinet, Zhou said but gave no further details.
